title: Request fanout attenuation and resilience guardrails
author: Elena Rodriguez
content:
Overview

This document defines Redwood's standards and recommended patterns for controlling request fanout, attenuating amplification effects, and providing resilient graceful degradation across API, infra, and model-serving layers. It unifies API semantics, infra-level controls, and observability signals so teams can safely expose multi-target requests (fanout) without risking cascading failures or large cost spikes.

Goals

- Limit unbounded amplification from single client requests (e.g., one client -> many model/auxiliary calls).
- Ensure predictable cost/latency profiles under bursty or adversarial traffic.
- Provide standard, interoperable controls for graceful degradation: partial responses, early-exit, and failure domains.
- Tie telemetry and SLOs to attenuation behavior so automated policies can act safely.

Scope

Applies to: API gateway, edge & ingress proxies, orchestration layer that fans out to model variants or auxiliary services (search, rerank, tool calls), and model-serving runtime. Not covered: client SDK behavior beyond suggested headers.

Design principles

1. Fail fast where impact is unbounded: Prefer rejecting or attenuating requests early when amplification risk cannot be bounded.
2. Explicit budget per request: Every request carries a request budget (tokens, RPCs, compute-units) conveyed through headers and enforced through gateways and router tiers.
3. Observables-first: Each attenuation point must emit an event with reason, decision (attenuate/allow), and the budget delta.
4. Composability: Attenuation controls are layered and orthogonal (client hints, gateway caps, model runtime early-exit).

API-level contract

- Request budget header: X-RW-Req-Budget (integer, compute-units). Default if absent: 100 compute-units.
- Max-fanout header: X-RW-Max-Fanout (integer). Gateway will reject requests that request fanout beyond allowed per-plan limits.
- Partial-response mode: X-RW-Partial-Mode (values: none|partial-keys|summary). If partial allowed, backends may return summarized or partial content.
- Failure-hint header: X-RW-Failure-Mode (values: retryable|fail-fast|fallback-preferred). This is advisory; enforcement is infra-driven.

Example request headers:

curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'X-RW-Req-Budget: 150' \
  -H 'X-RW-Max-Fanout: 10' \
  -H 'X-RW-Partial-Mode: summary' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/compose

Infra controls and runtime enforcement

Table: key attenuation controls and recommended defaults

| Control | Enforcement point | Default / recommended value | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Per-request compute budget | Edge gateway + router | 100 compute-units (soft), 300 (hard for enterprise) | Edge team |
| Fanout cap | Gateway + router | 12 parallel targets per request | Router team |
| Staggered fanout window | Router | 200ms jitter spread for parallel calls >4 | Runtime team |
| Early-exit threshold | Model-serving runtime | Stop at 0.6 quality score drop or 80% token budget | Runtime team |
| Cumulative cost guard | Billing-middleware | Reject if projected spend > monthly quota slice | Finance/Quota service |

Notes: compute-units are an internal abstraction that combines expected token cost, KV cache usage, and auxiliary RPC counts. Each service publishes a compute-unit price in the service catalog.

Attenuation strategies (patterns)

1) Fanout cap and tiering
- Gate maximum parallel targets at edge based on plan (free/dev/prod) and request budget.
- Tiered behavior: below 25% budget use full parallelism; 25–75% use staggered; above 75% reject or require partial mode.

2) Staggered concurrency (jittered waterfall)
- When making many parallel backend calls (search + rerank + tool call), the router adds jitter and progressive concurrency windows to smooth spikes.
- Example: 8 targets -> start 2, after 50ms start 3 more, remaining after next 150ms.

3) Early-exit and progressive refinement
- Model-serving runtime supports returning intermediate summaries or truncated outputs with confidence signals. 
- Clients are encouraged to accept X-RW-Partial-Mode to enable progressive refinement.

4) Aggregation and sampling as amplification antidotes
- For duplicate or similar fanout targets, combine queries server-side (e.g., batch or multi-query).
- When cost risk is high, sample 50% of non-critical targets and mark response with attenuation.reason = sampled.

Observability and SLOs

Every attenuation decision must emit the following telemetry fields (minimum):
- request_id, route, attenuation_point (edge|router|runtime), decision (allow|attenuate|reject), budget_before, budget_after, reason_code, downstream_targets, latency_ms.

SLOs and alerts:
- Attenuation rate: <= 2% of production requests should be attenuated for cost reasons under baseline traffic. Alert if > 5% sustained over 15m.
- Amplification spikes: Alert when median downstream_targets per request > baseline+3*stdev for 5m.
- Partial-response quality regression: If average downstream eval score for partial responses falls below baseline by 10%, trigger regression alert tied to quality-monitoring.

Operational playbook (incident triage)

1) Detection: Alert fires for amplification spike or high attenuation rate.
2) Initial triage (5 min): Identify impacted routes and top client tokens. Escalate to Router and Edge on-call.
3) Containment (10 min): Apply emergency fanout cap through router feature-flag (binary knob), or engage plan-level hard caps.
4) Mitigation (30 min): Enable partial-response mode for affected routes; activate cached-response fallback; enable sample-only mode (reduce noncritical fanout).
5) Root-cause (2–8 hours): Run request sampling and golden-trace correlation to find bad clients or regression in model cost-profile.
6) Remediation: Deploy model artifact rollback, adjust compute-unit pricing, or issue client rate-limits.

Rollout checklist for new fanout-enabled API

1. Define compute-unit cost for every backend target and publish in service catalog.
2. Add budget headers and client SDK support for X-RW-Req-Budget and X-RW-Partial-Mode.
3. Implement edge-level soft caps with clear rejection reasons (429 + X-RW-Attenuation-Reason).
4. Emit attenuation telemetry events and validate in staging ingestion.
5. Run chaos tests simulating client bursts and confirm SLOs (latency, cost, error budget) remain within thresholds.
6. Documentation and customer communication (if plan limits change).

Configuration example (router agent YAML snippet)

agent:
  name: router-attenuation-agent
  fanout:
    default_max_parallel: 12
    stagger_windows_ms: [50,150]
    soft_budget_threshold: 0.75
    enforce_partial_header: true
  telemetry:
    emit_attenuation_events: true
    sample_rate: 1.0

Ownership and governance

- Edge team: validate and enforce plan-level caps; return standard attenuation response codes.
- Router team: implement staggered fanout, budget enforcement, and per-route policies.
- Runtime team: expose early-exit APIs and confidence signals; expose cost telemetry.
- Observability: define attenuation event schema, maintain dashboards and alerting runbooks.
- Product/Finance: set default compute-unit pricing per model/service and define plan caps.

Compatibility notes and backwards-compatibility

- Clients that do not supply X-RW-Req-Budget will use the default. A migration window of 90 days is required before changing defaults.
- If X-RW-Partial-Mode is absent, systems assume partial-mode=none and will apply stricter caps.

Security and privacy considerations

- Attenuation telemetry must avoid logging prompt text; include only hashed prompt fingerprints where needed.
- When sampling requests for RCA, ensure PII redaction and adherence to retention policies.

Appendix: standard attenuation reason codes

- ATTN_OVER_FANOUT_CAP: request exceeds allowed parallel targets
- ATTN_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: request compute budget would be exceeded
- ATTN_SAMPLING: non-critical targets sampled down to reduce cost
- ATTN_PARTIAL_OK: request accepted but returned partial response per client preference
- ATTN_REJECT_PLAN: request exceeds plan-level contractual limits

Related artifacts and references

- See /confluence/architecture-and-standards/infra-standards/queue-smoothing-and-throttling-safeguards-2026 for queueing interactions.
- Runtime early-exit contract: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/deterministic-inference-and-reproducibility-standards-2026

Questions and feedback

For design questions or to request a non-default plan cap, contact the Edge team or open a PR on the attenuation-agent repo.
